dedupe_keys.name: crop expansion development potential index dpi global 1 km oakleaf kennedy kiesecker and co authors

description: A global 1 km raster that ranks all land suitable for crop expansion from just above 0 (minimal) to 1 (highest). The figshare description says the index is a weighted summary of three criteria: mean potential yield of ten crops (barley, cassava, maize, oil palm, rapeseed, rice, sugarcane, sorghum, soybean and wheat), market accessibility and land supply elasticity, with weights from an Analytic Hierarchy Process pairwise comparison. The package also holds a classified version of the index, a classified uncertainty layer, sensitivity tables for all criteria and a full description of constraints and criteria. It was created by James R. Oakleaf, Christina M. Kennedy, Sharon Baruch-Mordo, James S. Gerber, Paul C. West, Justin A. Johnson and Joseph Kiesecker, issued in 2019 and updated in March 2020, and is a downloadable package of about 185 MB, free under CC0 1.0. Coverage is global land at 1 km. Caveats: file formats are not listed in the metadata read, and the weights are expert choices. For simulation it shows where market access and yield make new cropland likely, so planners can test where rural roads, storage and irrigation will be needed. Related catalogue records include the global agricultural expansion potential maps at 300 m and LS-500 global cropland suitability.
